theTwelveCorpusClaim.result: Twelve for twelve. Every one is CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED with binds NOTHING and NOT-AUTHORED present, and every filed claude2 verdict reads ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. Zero sub-claim failures. FC-RO resolves to v3 — v1 accepted, v2 rejected at 1 blocker, v3 accepted — so the family's live member is the accepted one.
theTwelveCorpusClaim.theShapeQuestionIRaisedElsewhere: Three of the twelve carry no initialStates array: doctor-fc-schema uses namedGoldens with nineteen entries, doctor-fc-d9 uses namedSets with seven, doctor-fc-remediation uses namedUnpopulatable with six. I checked before treating that as emptiness, and it is not — each names a real inventory shaped to its class. The join's phrase is 'INPUT/initial-state corpora' and v6's is 'INPUT/initial-state catalogs', neither of which claims a uniform key. This family also does not use the stateNamed convention at all: doctor-fc-nc's two entries carry consentClass, sentinel, trace and verbatimFromV4 instead. It is a different document family from the g16/g21/g22/g23/g25/g27 input corpora, and the standards question I raised at G18 does not transfer to it unexamined.
theTwelveCorpusClaim.andNoExactByteIntentClaimIsMade: The role string that produced CLAUDE-G18LJ-V2-SF1 — 'Named initial states from live exactByteIntent' — does not appear in this artifact at all. There is no input-corpus basedOn entry; the measurement is consumed from v6.

A downstream join cannot be faulted for relying on a recorded verdict, and I will not use this review to reverse two verdicts I did not author and whose subjects are not my subject.
disclosureOnTwoOfTheTwelve.whyTheCoordinatorNeedsIt: The record this join reads and measurements I performed disagree on two of the twelve corpora that discharge OBL-G12-INPUT-CORPUS. If either of my unfiled findings is correct, the closure of that obligation rests in part on corpora with an open SHOULD-FIX. That is a question about the record, not about this artifact, and it cannot be settled while my verdicts have nowhere to land. This is the strongest instance yet of why the filing-path question matters.
disclosureOnTwoOfTheTwelve.whatIAmNotAsserting: I am not asserting my two verdicts are right and the filed ones wrong. I am asserting that two independent measurements exist, they disagree, and only one side is on the record.

coordinatorSummary: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. Twenty-eight attacks run, none landed. Custody holds: subject 0b68c98b at 0444, 13844 bytes, unmoved; HEAD never left 5d5d778 and recordedInputs.HEAD equals the top-level head; required-now 26 of 26; file 08 and COORD unmodified and matching their pins; all eleven recordedInputs files reproduce with basedOn cross-checked at zero disagreements. The shortfall test resolves as the mirror of a case I ruled on this morning. G12 v4's leftoverDesignRemainingOnDR114 enumerates nine and the join names eight, omitting OBL-G21-HARNESS-SPEC; doctor-actor-leftover-join.v6 is the live DR-114 ledger and its summary.leftoverDesign is exactly those eight, with OBL-G21-HARNESS-SPEC sitting at leftoverDesign false because a G21 specification now exists. That is the precise reciprocal of g21-leftover-join.v2, whose harness list carried OBL-G12-HARNESS-SPEC and which named eight. Both harness enumerations are stale about each other and the live ledger is current in both directions, so ruling the same way here is the rule tested against its own reciprocal. The twelve-corpus claim was verified corpus by corpus rather than read. I mapped one corpus to each of the twelve FC classes v6 names and opened each: twelve for twelve on CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, binds NOTHING, NOT-AUTHORED present, and filed claude2 verdict ACCEPT 0/0, with FC-RO correctly resolving to v3 after its v2 was rejected. Three of the twelve carry no initialStates array, which I checked before treating as emptiness: schema holds nineteen namedGoldens, d9 seven namedSets, remediation six namedUnpopulatable. This family does not use the stateNamed convention at all, so the standards question I raised at G18 does not transfer to it unexamined, and the role string that produced that finding does not appear here at all. One disclosure is material and is not a defect of this artifact. Two of the twelve corpora on which OBL-G12-INPUT-CORPUS rests — doctor-fc-nc-input-corpus.v1 and doctor-fc-hostile-input-corpus.v1 — carry filed verdicts of ACCEPT 0/0 authored by another Claude-2-lane reviewer, at paths where I hold completed but unfiled verdicts of REJECT at 1 SHOULD-FIX. The join cites the filed record and the filed record says ACCEPT, so its claim is true as measured. But the record and an independent measurement disagree on two corpora that help close an obligation, and only one side is on the record. I declined to import that as a finding, because it would let a downstream review reverse verdicts I did not author on subjects that are not mine — the same move I refused at G18 when the conflict was with my own earlier acceptance. It cannot be settled while those verdicts have nowhere to land. The rest holds. OBL-DOCTOR-FX-AUTHORING stays leftoverDesign true and is the sole member of summary.leftoverDesign; it is also true on DR-114 at v6, and the join discloses that rather than displacing it, so the two-join overlap is coherent. Cell [7] of the DR-G12 row is OPEN and cell [4] is byte-identical to liveGateOwners; the twelve FC classes come from G12 v4's namedCorpusNotAuthored, not from file 08's harness cell, which holds different text. The predecessor role's 'named-catalog' — the exact wording I filed as a defect at G23 — is correct here, because G12 has both the catalog artifact and the obligation, pinned and accepted. Eight of eight gate joins now assert leftoverDesignClosedIfAcceptedAndRecorded exactly when their harness carries it. The successor diff is the tightest yet: five obligations to six, one added, none removed, and no obligation modified in any field, with doesNot byte-identical at fourteen entries.
